turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. I have twenty minutes, so start with who decided that, and when.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero rests on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.

I'm writing those times down. Students draft in one place and paste into another, so a document that starts late tells me where it was typed, not who wrote it. And before you entered anything, did you sit down with Owen and ask him?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.

Fine, the dates stand for now. Whatever happens with this essay, it stays off his record and it stays quiet, nothing in front of his class. And you still haven't told me whether anyone heard Owen before that zero went in.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Give me the screen. Seventeen-year-olds misremember lines and pin them on the wrong act every day, Hale; one bad quotation is a careless citation, not proof of anything.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I've searched it, and it isn't there. That tells me the line isn't Shakespeare's; it doesn't tell me anything about Owen. So say plainly what you're putting on the table.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.

Forty minutes in class with no book open against a take-home with the whole play in front of him; of course one has quotations and the other doesn't. And I asked you a question you've now stepped around twice: what are you proposing?

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

Okay, to put this behind him, Owen does the rewrite, under 4.4, privately. Tonight's email says the rewrite mark replaces the zero, nothing goes on his record or to the office, and you put in writing that the zero went in before anyone called home. Then you tell me when and where, and Owen hears it from you, not from his phone.
Will he do it?
He'll do it. Schedule it soon, because his scholarship applications close December 1, and I'm not watching another deadline pass while this school sorts itself out.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Today you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, not in front of his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still require your written acknowledgment that the zero was entered before anyone contacted me, the time and place of the rewrite before his December 1 scholarship deadline, and that you tell Owen yourself. I expect your written confirmation tonight, as you promised.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight, an acknowledgment that the zero went in before you called home, and the rewrite scheduled before December 1; this is the fair outcome.
What moved her: You showed the version history with exact times and then answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by offering to check any other file's dates, because she trusts dated documents she can verify herself.
What cost ground: You never answered her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero and went to the next document instead, which made her sharper even though she didn't lose a position.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing late on the night before it was due, close to the kind of night she was afraid of; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether anyone sat down with Owen before the zero went in, answer that directly and honestly before showing the quotation evidence.
